title: How to spot a fake 'successful' store (4 checks)
caption: That 'six-figure store' screenshot proves nothing. 4 free checks in 5 minutes: ads, reviews, socials, traffic. Verify before you copy anyone. #dropshipping #ecommercetruth #shopify #ecommercetips

beats.headline: Six figures? | *Prove* it.
beats.say: That store someone flexed as a six-figure winner? It might not make a *single* sale. [surprise-oh]

beats.headline: Check before you *copy*
beats.say: Before you copy any store, run these four *checks.* Takes five minutes.

beats.headline: The last one | tells the *truth.*
beats.say: Four checks. The last one tells the *truth.*
Check one. *Open* the Meta Ad Library and type the store name. A real winner is running ads right now. Zero active ads? *Red* flag.
Check two, the reviews. Two hundred reviews from the same week, all five stars, no photos? *Fake.* Real reviews are spread out, with photos, and a few honest complaints.
Check three, their socials. Big follower count, but *every* comment is just an emoji? Probably bought. *Look* for questions. Real buyers ask about sizing and shipping.
Check four. Paste the link into any free traffic estimator. Claiming a hundred grand a month on four hundred *visitors?* The *math* doesn't work.

visual.prompt: A store gets ~400 visits a month. At 2% conversion and a $35 average order, what's its max monthly revenue?

beats.say: Not sure? *Ask* any AI. Give it the traffic, a two percent conversion rate, and the price. Then ask: what's the most this store could really make?

beats.label: Run the 4 checks
beats.headline: Follow for *more*
beats.say: *Save* these four checks, and follow for honest e-commerce.
